title: Token Surge Safeguard: Microbenchmark for TPS Stability and p95 Regression Detection
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a compact microbenchmark harness that emulates realistic token surge patterns (adversarial bursts + diurnal variance) against core LLMs to validate tokens-per-second (TPS) stability and detect p95 latency regressions early. The harness should produce deterministic fingerprints, support multiple concurrency profiles, include KV-cache warmup scenarios, and integrate with our regression detector and Alerting/Canary pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark can reproduce 5 canonical surge scenarios (sustained ramp, microburst, burst+backoff, staggered concurrency, persistent tail-pressure) against 3 core models
Automated p95 change-point detection triggers alerts when deviation > 12% from baseline with fewer than 10 false positives in 100 runs
Bench supports KV-cache cold, partial-warmed, and fully-warmed runs and reports separate TPS/p95 per cache state
Outputs deterministic run fingerprints and artifact links suitable for CI artifacts (bench traces, perf flamegraphs, summary CSV)
Integration: results land in the throughput dashboard and can be consumed by canary gating (shadow-run) before rollouts
implementation_notes: 2026-02-12: spike completed — validated synthetic burst generator parameters against production traces (sampled from token-velocity logs)

2026-03-08: performance artifacts wired into perf-dashboard ingestion; short-term storage on s3://redwood-bench-archives/token-surge/

testing_plan: Run full suite nightly against stable model versions (A/B/C) with seeded RNG for reproducibility. For each run capture: token throughput by 1s buckets, p50/p95/p99 latency, KV hit-rate, GPU util, and kernel selection logs. Use bootstrapped baselines to compute significance and surface regression summaries to the throughput dashboard. Manual review for first 10 CI failures to tune thresholds.
risks: False positives due to non-deterministic infra noise (mitigation: multiple repeats and bootstrap-confidence intervals)
Bench-induced load could interfere with Shared QA infra (mitigation: isolated GPU pools and rate-limited runner accounts)
Large artifact volume (traces/metrics) increasing storage costs (mitigation: aggressive retention + summary artifacts)
Model-level variability across providers (we will annotate runs by region/hardware)
notes: Design trade-off: lightweight deterministic workloads vs full production replay. Chose compact synthetic scenarios to enable fast CI feedback while keeping one periodic production-replay job (weekly)
PM feedback (Sofia Patel): prioritize integration with canary gating over extensive feature matrix in MVP
Design feedback (Liam O'Connor): include explicit warmup handshake and configurable KV-cache time-to-live for partial-warm profiles
Action item: add noise-injection toggle to simulate intermittent infra stalls (assigned to ENG-334779)
observability_requirements: Per-second token counters with 99th percentile retention for 30 days
Run-level trace IDs that correlate bench events with GPU kernel logs
Auto-generated summary CSV and flamegraphs posted as CI artifacts
Alerting hook: canary-regression-channel with run fingerprint and run URL
rollout_plan: 1) Merge MVP to benchmarks and enable nightly runs for master. 2) Wire results to perf-dashboard and enable simple alerting (EWMA threshold) in canary shadow pipeline for internal rollouts. 3) After 2 weeks of stable noise levels, promote alert to blocking canary gate for runtime-1.22 rollouts. 4) Iterate thresholds based on false-positive telemetry and stakeholder feedback.
